findings.description: `createBooking` looks up a booking using the caller-controlled `idempotencyKey` instead of the `bookingId` saved in the caller’s idempotency record, then returns any match without checking its owner. On a same-body replay, an ordinary key misses and creates another booking with a `201` response, while a key matching another user’s booking ID returns that user’s full booking instead of the caller’s recorded booking.

evidence.explanation: The request header supplies the key, and idempotency records are scoped by user and key, but bookings are stored in a global map indexed by their generated IDs. On a matching-fingerprint replay, looking up the key rather than the ID saved in the record either misses and falls through to booking creation, which the POST route returns with `201`, or finds another user’s booking and returns it directly; unlike the GET route, the POST route does not check ownership.

findings.title: Booking replays expose another user's data
